issue: #390 follow-up — task.rs sat 26 lines over the 500-line limit on main, and no CI lane could see it
scope_note: A smaller change than the #390 receipts, and the receipt is scoped to match rather than padded to look like them. Two claims, not forty-three. What did NOT run is named under lanes_not_run — the point of a receipt is that a reader can tell the difference between a lane that passed and a lane that was skipped.

claims.claim: Splitting src/resources/task.rs into task/{mod,helpers,check,apply,query}.rs changes no behaviour.
claims.how_tested: Sorted the non-import, non-module-doc lines of origin/main:src/resources/task.rs and of the four new files and diffed them. Result: exactly three differing lines, all `fn X` -> `pub(super) fn X` (service_rid, timeout_wrapped, pipeline_script), which sibling submodules must now call across a module boundary. Every other byte identical, so no generated shell script can differ.

claims.claim: No CI lane enforced the 500-line limit, so PR #397 landed task.rs at 530 lines fully green.
claims.how_tested: Searched every file in .github/workflows for a max-lines/comply/file-health check: none exists; the only hits for `wc -l` count tarballs and commits. Confirmed a6a37c52 took the file 481 -> 530 and 8741b685 trimmed it to 526, both over the limit, with PR #397 merged on a green run.

falsification.method: The new CI step was extracted from lint.yml with a YAML parser and run as a standalone script against real git history in throwaway worktrees, so each case is the actual shipped shell, not a paraphrase.

cases.observed: File health OK, exit 0 — the split shrinks every file

cases.setup: a6a37c52 vs its own parent (the commit that slipped through)

cases.observed: (0 -> 600), exit 1 — and NOT the exit 128 the first draft produced

cases.setup: rename a 530-line file and add one line
cases.observed: (530 -> 531), exit 1 — `before` read from the OLD path
File health OK, exit 0 — no false positive on a move

defects_these_cases_caught: T3 caught a hard failure in my own first draft: `before=$(git cat-file -p "$BASE:$f" 2>/dev/null | wc -l)` reads as total but under `set -euo pipefail` an absent path makes git exit 128, pipefail propagates it, and the ASSIGNMENT itself trips `set -e`. The job would have died 128 on the first newly-added .rs file in any PR. Verified in isolation: the line after the assignment never printed, exit 128.
T4/T6 caught the rename and spaced-path holes agy reported.

agy_teamwork.split_verdict: SHIP — independently re-derived the sorted-body diff and agreed the move is pure
findings_accepted: pipefail abort on new files (I had found this independently minutes earlier; agy confirmed it)

PR base drift: pull_request.base.sha is the tip when the webhook fired, so main's growth is billed to this PR. agy's fix (the merge commit's first parent) is strictly better than mine (git merge-base), because base.sha is already an ancestor of the merge commit and merge-base therefore returns base.sha unchanged — my fix was a no-op. Adopted agy's.
a multi-commit push to main only compares HEAD~1, the parent of the LAST commit
a path containing a space is quoted by git and silently skipped by [ -f "$f" ]
agy_teamwork.note: All five were real. This lane is the reason the job ships correct; the test suite was green throughout and proved nothing about any of them.

gates.bashrs: 0 errors on the extracted CI step (7 warnings, 17 info, all style)

lanes_not_run.crux_competitive_survey: NOT RUN. A max-lines ratchet is not a design space worth surveying — the rule already exists in this repo's CLAUDE.md and its pre-commit hook, and this change only moves enforcement to where it can block a merge. Recorded as skipped rather than quietly omitted.
lanes_not_run.three_refuter_panel: NOT RUN as a formal 3-lens panel. One adversarial lane ran (agy /teamwork) and it returned DO-NOT-SHIP with five findings, all accepted. Claiming a panel that did not sit would be the exact failure this receipt exists to prevent.
lanes_not_run.pmat_mcp: NOT RUN on this change; the split adds no new logic to grade and clippy/fmt/TDG-baseline all ran.

known_limits: The gate reads `before` with `wc -l`, which counts newlines: a file with no trailing newline is undercounted by one. The pre-commit hook has the same behaviour, so the two agree.
A copy (C) is treated as a new file, so copying a 600-line file fails the gate. That is arguably correct and is not tested.

T5 was initially run in a worktree already polluted by T4's rename and reported a false `(0 -> 530)`. Re-run clean in a fresh worktree, it passes. The first run is recorded here because a receipt that hides its own bad tests is worthless.
gate_bug_found_in_passing: scripts/quorum-gate.sh resolves .quorum/<branch>.json from the WORKING TREE, not from the ref being pushed. Pushing branch B while checked out on branch A reports B's receipt as missing even though it exists on B. Not fixed here; filed as a follow-up.
